scope: F600 F5 event/stream/lifecycle timing contracts; Smith-py train only; four competition repositories excluded.
selection_policy: Explicit train-only F5 mechanism sources with production-to-consumption-to-end event-sequence observations; single-point values demoted to S/G and SSE-string escapes rejected during review.

mechanism_evidence.causal_contract: Async action registration must append in order so begin runs before retry checks; prepending reverses the begin-retry-post execution chain.
retry_all must require every sub-predicate; a single success must not retry while mixed outcomes follow all/any truth tables. Using any retries when only one predicate fires.

Outcome construction must wrap results as results and exceptions as exceptions so downstream predicates inspect the right branch; swapping the branches and returning None breaks the produce-inspect-decide chain.
stop_any must keep every stop so the first firing stop ends retries. Dropping the first stop delays the attempt-stop-end chain.
The never-stop predicate must stay false for every attempt so retries continue until other stops fire. Returning true stops the first attempt-sleep-end cycle immediately.
Begin attempts one through four with stop_after_attempt(3). The stop predicate must receive the live retry state so early attempts continue and later attempts stop.
stop_any must fire when any sub-stop fires so the earliest deadline ends retries; requiring all stops delays the attempt-stop-end chain to the latest deadline.
Random-exponential wait must draw uniformly between min and the exponential high for each attempt. Using an undefined bound breaks the attempt-sleep-end chain.
Chained waits must keep stage order so early attempts use the first stage and late attempts reuse the last. Reversing stages swaps early/late sleeps across the attempt-sleep-end chain.
retry_if_not_result must keep the predicate polarity so refuting results retry and matching results stop; negating at registration inverts every decision across the outcome-decision chain.
stop_before_delay must keep the exact max seconds so the pre-sleep deadline check fires on time; shaving one second stops every cycle early across the attempt-time-stop chain.
stop_after_delay must keep the exact max seconds so the deadline fires on time; taking abs plus a tenth delays every stop decision across the attempt-time-stop chain.
Incrementing wait must keep start/increment/max in order so attempt sleeps grow linearly and cap at max. Rotating the three arguments corrupts the attempt-sleep-end chain.
stop_after_attempt must keep the exact max count so the Nth attempt stops; decrementing at registration stops every cycle one attempt early across the attempt-stop-end chain.

Jittered exponential wait must keep initial/max/exp_base/jitter roles so sleeps grow exponentially within bounds; rotating the four arguments collapses every sleep to the cap across the attempt-sleep-end chain.
The never-retry gate must reject every outcome so nothing retries; gating on a positive attempt number retries every cycle across the outcome-decision chain.
Registering iteration actions must append each action exactly once in order; duplicating the first and dropping the rest corrupts the begin-retry-post execution chain.
Jittered waits must add the jitter to the exponential and clamp into range; subtracting and clamping outside collapses every sleep to zero across the attempt-sleep-end chain.

Exponential wait must keep a positive multiplier and base so sleeps double within bounds; negating the multiplier and bumping the base collapses every sleep to zero across the attempt-sleep-end chain.
stop_all must require every sub-stop so the latest deadline governs; using any ends at the earliest deadline across the attempt-stop-end chain.

stop_after_attempt must fire once the attempt number reaches the max so the final attempt ends the cycle; requiring strictly more runs every schedule one attempt long across the attempt-stop-end chain.

A fresh call with no outcome must reset iteration state before selecting DoAttempt; a failed TryAgain outcome must take the explicit-retry branch. Resetting after reading the outcome corrupts the branch.
Blocking iteration must begin a new call and build attempt state before the first DoAttempt. Beginning after the loop leaves attempt_number/idle uninitialized for the first attempt-sleep-end cycle.

After a non-stopping decision the controller must schedule sleep, advance idle_for and attempt_number, then emit DoSleep; after a stopping decision it must surface the retry error. The rewrite drops next-attempt accounting.

Closing must flush, close the fd, wait for kernel status, terminate only if alive, then mark fd -1 and closed. Moving flush outside and gating fd assignment on aliveness raises on clean exits instead of closing.
Reading the echo flag must report the actual terminal state after each set call; returning the inverted flag from the wrong bit breaks the set-poll-detect chain.
waitnoecho must report true once echo clears and false on timeout expiry; inverting both outcomes breaks the spawn-poll-detect chain for password prompts.

Waiting on a live child must block in waitpid and return its status; waiting on a reaped child must return the cached status. Inverting the branch returns None immediately and blocks forever on dead children.
Wait must check aliveness and reap via waitpid before interpreting the status word. Reading an unassigned status breaks the spawn-wait-reap chain with an unbound variable.
A child killed by a signal must report not-alive with exitstatus None, the signal number, and terminated true. Dropping those assignments leaves stale exit state across the spawn-signal-reap chain.
Waiting for no-echo must poll the echo flag until it clears or the timeout expires; deleting the poll loop returns None immediately, breaking the spawn-poll-detect chain.
Update must queue the supplied row so the exit flush persists it. Queuing None breaks the produce-queue-flush chain and crashes grouping.
Entering a chunked writer must return the writer so queued rows can be added before the exit flush. Returning None breaks the enter-produce-flush chain.
Exiting a chunked writer must flush queued rows on both clean and exceptional exits. Skipping the flush on clean exits loses the produce-flush-persist chain.

Update flush must group queued rows by key sets so same-schema rows persist in one call; grouping by values splits every row and persists key lists instead of rows across the queue-flush-persist chain.
Conditional insert must persist a missing row and skip an existing one by key; always returning false without inserting loses the check-persist-read chain.

Update flush must invoke the callback on queued rows, sort and group by keys into update_many calls, then clear the queue; clearing first persists nothing and reports empty across the queue-flush-persist chain.
Bulk update must build and execute the update statement for every full chunk and the tail; deleting the statement leaves rows unpersisted across the produce-execute-read chain.
Bulk update must iterate every supplied row into chunks for execution; deleting the loop persists nothing across the produce-execute-read chain.
Bulk insert must sync columns from all rows then persist every row in order; syncing only the first row and reordering drops columns and rows across the produce-persist-read chain.
